title: Risk scratch stations — SOC2 prep fragments
content:
Quick notes dump — working through SOC2 control threads and what we actually have vs what auditors will ask for. Mostly rough, leaving breadcrumbs to tidy later.

High level hypothesis: we have the pieces but scattered across hosts, console, and private deployment checklists. Need to collate EVIDENCE artifacts and owners for each cc.

Open questions / reminders:
- Access reviews: when was last org-wide identity churn? Need evidence of quarterly review (ticket + approval). Look for: IDP audit logs (Okta), admin role list export (okta-admins.csv), ticket referencing 2025-11 restructure. -> JIRA-SEC-881 may cover some.
- Key management: Private deployments use customer KMS. For hosted, who rotates root keys and where are rotation records? Check kms-ops runbook and rotation scripts in infra repo.
- Backup verification: we snapshot model artifacts daily. Do we have a tested restore report? I think we ran a restore test Q4 2025 but not documented. Find runbook entry + Slack thread #runbooks-restore (search: "restore drill nov25").
- Change control: PR approvals are in GitHub but auditors want evidence of review + rollback plan. We have github + deploy tags, but need a clear timeline export for the auditor (example CSV).

Control mapping sketch (very rough):
- CC6 (Logical & Physical Access): Okta groups + SSO logs + SRE access spreadsheet. Evidence = okta-export.csv, bastion access logs, jumpbox session traces. Owner: Lina (infra).
- CC7 (Change management): GitHub PRs, CI pipeline run IDs, deployment tags, rollbacks. Evidence = PR-IDs + CI run URLs. Owner: Rohan (platform eng).
- CC10 (System operations): Incident tickets + postmortems, pager duty runbooks, maintenance windows calendar. Evidence = incidents/PMR docs. Owner: Zoe (trust-ops).

Evidence shorthand I need to assemble (to collect into a zip):
- identity-review-2025Q4.csv (from Okta)
- admin-role-export-202602.csv
- kms-rotation-log-2025-2026.txt
- restore-drill-report-2025-11.md
- sample-PR-timeline-202601.csv (generate via GH API)
- incident-list-12mo.csv and 2 sample PMs (inc-2025-09, inc-2026-01)

Immediate TODOs (prioritized):
1) Pull Okta export, tag owners + redact emails where required (Zoe) — due 2026-03-05.
2) Ask infra (Lina) for bastion session traces and confirm retention window.
3) Get CI/GH export for last 6 months showing code reviews + deploy timestamps (Rohan).
4) Search Slack for restore drill thread; if missing, schedule a quick restore verification next week (owner: Zoe).

Potential auditor questions we should pre-answer (brain-dump):
- Who can approve a production model change? Show flow: PR -> CODEOWNERS -> staging integration tests -> canary rollout -> manual approval for full rollout. Provide sample PR IDs and approval comments.
- How do you ensure customer data isolation for private deployments? Answer: VPC-only routing + optional customer KMS + per-customer network ACLs; need architecture diagram + checklist.
- Where are logs retained and how long? We need a single doc listing retention across subsystems (console logs, inference runtime, billing events).

Notes to self: keep this file as the central scratchpad for the next 2 weeks. After collating evidence, create a prettier pack in shared_drives/company/misc/soc2-evidence-bundle-v1.zip and move final docs to shared_drives/security-and-compliance.

Random reminders: capture linear ticket IDs for 'evidence exports' request; add a template CSV for audit timeline. Create a tiny script to fetch GH PR metadata (PR id, author, reviewers, merged_at) to save manual effort.

Fragmented brainstorm — auditor-friendly checklist items (short):
- list of privileged users + recent approvals
- one-page change control narrative + example PR
- restore test report + screenshots
- KMS rotation proof + who performed rotation
- incident response timeline + major PM

End of dump. Will tidy into structured mapping file next pass.

Slack references: #trust-ops, #infra-runbooks, #audit-prep.

Signature: z/p (Zoe) — quick and messy, come back later to make formal.
